title: Lesson with MoistCr1tikal - Predicting The Future

moves.spoken: He'll play e4 for sure — he plays it nearly every game — and you respond with e5.
Then he almost always plays the knight to f3, so that's to be expected.
And you respond with the knight to c6. He plays the same opening every single time,
so we can actually prepare for him. He plays what's called the Scotch — the move d4.
Now in a couple of games he played the bishop to c4, the Italian, so let me show you a
few moves here just to be sure. He's threatening the f7-pawn — do you know what to do as Black? Well, it's

actually defended by the king, so he's not really threatening it; you can just develop symmetrically with the bishop to c5. Just because he puts pressure on it doesn't mean you have to go out of your way to defend it.
So you play the bishop to c5, he castles, and now you just develop
the knight to f6. In one of the games that reached this position he played d4,
which at a low level is a good opening. He goes d4 — this looks like a blunder, but you should be seeing something: this is
a trap. If you take it with the pawn, he
has the move e5, with a very nasty attack against your knight.
If you take with the knight, he takes
back on e5. But there's one piece you can

take with that doesn't allow him to do anything — take the pawn on d4 with the bishop, not the knight and not the queen. You take with the bishop, he takes back, you take the knight, and he cannot recapture, because that pawn is defended by your other two pieces. The line goes f4, d6, and it holds — he's not going to know it this deep.
